lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about buses and trains.
Sam, how do you go to work?
By bus. The bus is slow, but I like it. Every day I ask, "Where is the bus stop?"
Every day?
Yes. My bus stop moves. Yesterday it was near the shop. Today it is near the school.
[laugh] Bus stops do not move, Sam. You move!
Maybe. I wait for the bus on the wrong road, the wrong street. Then I get on the bus. I ask, "How much is a ticket?" The driver says, "One manat." Every day, one manat.
And when do you get off?
When I see my office. Sometimes I am late. I say, "I'm late!" The driver says, "Sam, you are always late."
Come on, take a taxi. A taxi is fast, very quick.
A taxi is not cheap. A car is not cheap. Only the bus is cheap. And the bus is my friend.
A late friend. Bye for now!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is traffic and commuting.
Sam, tell us about yesterday.
Terrible. It was rush hour. The bus broke down in the middle of the road, and everybody got off.
Did the driver call someone?
He called his cousin. His cousin came with a bigger bus. And that bus broke down, too.
[laugh] So what did you do?
I called you. I said, "Sorry, I'm stuck in traffic." You said, "You are always stuck."
It's true. Every route in this city has a delay, no parking, and a station that is never on time.
A passenger next to me asked, "Is this seat free?" I said, "Yes. There is a reason." It was wet.
Sam! You let him sit in the wet?
He sat down on the wet seat. His face... Then the driver slowed down and said, "Next stop, please," but there was no next stop.
So you walked.
And I arrived before the bus. A great day. Please drop me off at the office next time.
I will not. See you next time!
Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is the daily commute. And my 7:40 bus.
Let's start with the facts. How long is your commute?
One hour and ten minutes. The distance is six kilometres. Congestion every morning, roadworks every afternoon, and a traffic jam in between.
That's bumper to bumper for six kilometres.
I know. And sometimes a cyclist overtakes the bus. I wave at him. He doesn't wave back.
You can find out which route is faster. Public transport is cheaper than a car, and the fare is only one manat.
But I have a back seat driver on the bus. An old lady behind me tells the driver, "Turn left. No, right."
Does he listen?
He pulls up right there and says, "Madam, you drive." She doesn't. And he holds up the whole street.
[laugh] And you, are you punctual?
In England I was. In Baku I missed the boat on punctuality. I'm the man who is always eight minutes late.
A question for our listeners: how do you get to work, and what do you do on the way?
Mine: I learn English on the bus, and I'm still late. See you next time!
